content.title: Orlando Magic at Philadelphia 76ers: Game Preview | Orlando Magic
content.text: The Orlando Magic have a clear path to the playoffs.Earn a victory in their next outing and they’re in.The Magic (45-37) will look to punch their ticket to the playoffs when they visit the Philadelphia 76ers (45-37) on Wednesday at 7:30 p.m. ET in the 7 vs. 8 NBA play-in game. The contest will air exclusively on Prime Video.“It’s a playoff game,” said Magic head coach Jamahl Mosley. “It’s a one-game hit. Our ability to focus on exactly what they do (and) exactly what we do well. Having played them a couple of times (this regular season), being able to hone in on what worked for us and what we need to clean up. Then, go from there.”The winner of this matchup will secure the seventh seed in the playoffs and earn a matchup with the Boston Celtics in the first round. The loser will have to host the Charlotte Hornets, who won the 9 vs. 10 play-in outing, for the opportunity to claim the eighth seed and square off with the Detroit Pistons. However, Orlando is hoping to handle its business tonight, so it doesn’t come down to a do-or-die matchup at Kia Center.“Guys are excited (and) guys are pissed off (that we didn’t beat Boston on Sunday for the chance to host this game),” said Magic forward Paolo Banchero. “Guys want to prove a point. So, I’m excited to see how we come out.”In order for Orlando to earn a victory, its defense will need to slow down Philadelphia’s Tyrese Maxey. The electrifying guard was top five in the NBA in scoring this season, pouring in 28.3 points per outing. He also finished top 20 in assists (6.6) and top 10 in steals (1.9) per contest among qualified players.“It starts with Maxey, (especially) with (Joel) Embiid being out,” Mosley explained. “His ability to create shots for himself, but also for others.”After being in and out of the lineup for the majority of the season, 76ers forward Paul George has started to round into form. The nine-time NBA All-Star averaged 21.0 points, 5.7 rebounds, 3.3 assists and 2.2 steals over the last 10 games of the 2025-26 campaign. He posted 20-plus points in six of those contests, including a season-high 39 points on April 1 against the Washington Wizards.Rookie VJ Edgecombe is also a threat to go off on any given night. The 6-foot-4 guard was one of two rookies in the NBA this season to average at least 16.0 points, 5.0 rebounds, and 4.0 assists per game. He finished the regular season ranking first in steals (1.4), third in scoring (16.0), third in assists (4.2) and seventh in rebounds (5.6) among first-year players.As a unit, the Sixers rank top six in both steals (9.1) and blocks (5.7) per contest, and use those stops to get out and run.“They play really physical,” said Magic forward Franz Wagner. “Obviously, we have to have a good game plan for Maxey. They have a lot of guys who like to attack from the perimeter. So, we have to make sure we play good team defense.”PLAYOFF PICTURE: As mentioned, the winner of tonight’s play-in game between Orlando and Philly will be the No. 7 seed in the playoffs and take on Boston in the first round. The loser will host Charlotte, who beat Miami in the 9 vs. 10 play-in game, on Friday at 7:30 p.m. ET. The winner of that contest will be the No. 8 seed and face Detroit in the first round. All play-in tournament games can be seen exclusively on Prime Video. No matter who advances from the play-in, Game 1 in Boston will be Sunday at 1 p.m. and will air on ABC and Game 1 in Detroit will be Sunday at 6:30 p.m. and will air on NBC/Peacock.IN AND OUT: Jett Howard (left ankle; sprain) and Jonathan Isaac (left knee; sprain) are both questionable for Orlando.For Philadelphia, Trendon Watford (illness) is probable, while Johni Broome (right knee; surgery recovery) and Joel Embiid (appendectomy surgery recovery) are out.QUOTES TO NOTE: “I think he thrives in those situations. I think we all feed off of that.” – Franz on Paolo’s performances in playoff games“We have to be locked in every night. Now, we’re on the road in a tough environment in the play-in game. We’ve got to respond and come out and play better.” – BancheroKEY STATS: Desmond Bane was one of only four players in the NBA to play and start in all 82 games this season. He is the first Orlando player since Dwight Howard in 2009-10 to start in all 82 games. He’s the ninth player in Magic history to accomplish the feat.HOW TO WATCH: Watch the contest on Prime Video.
